messages.author: 5b97a521f83fcfe0
messages.subject: simsem question
parts:
Hi all,

I have a question concerning the sim() function in the simsem package.

I tried the example provided in the function's documentation:

popModel <- "
f1 =~ 0.7*y1 + 0.7*y2 + 0.7*y3
f2 =~ 0.7*y4 + 0.7*y5 + 0.7*y6
f1 ~~ 1*f1
f2 ~~ 1*f2
f1 ~~ 0.5*f2
y1 ~~ 0.49*y1
y2 ~~ 0.49*y2
y3 ~~ 0.49*y3
y4 ~~ 0.49*y4
y5 ~~ 0.49*y5
y6 ~~ 0.49*y6
"

analysisModel <- "
f1 =~ y1 + y2 + y3
f2 =~ y4 + y5 + y6"

With the following code provided in the example it word, as expected, well
Output1 <- sim(5, model=analysisModel, n=200, generate=popModel, std.lv=TRUE, lavaanfun = "cfa")

However, I use try to pass the argument se = "none" to lavaan
Output2 <- sim(5, model=analysisModel, n=200, generate=popModel, std.lv=TRUE, lavaanfun = "cfa", se = "none")

there is the following error:
Error in names(se) <- lab : attempt to set an attribute on NULL

I do not need the stand errors, so I want to get rid of them to speed up the computation. Is this possible, or is there an error in the function?

Btw. I use R 4.0.2, lavaan 0.6-11, and simsem 0.5-16

Best regards,
Eric

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: simsem question
parts:
I don't think this is possible in the current version of simsem. se = "none returns a value of NULL for SEs when requested. The current formulation of the sim function assumes the each model has a vector of standard errors the same length as the number of parameters. If computing SEs really adds to the time needed one workaround right now would be to write a custom function to pass to the sim function (see the sim() help documentation for details). This function needs to return a vector of SEs, but you can just fill in NAs for those within the function without computing them. 

Alex
